tagline: Democratizing global investing through social trading and education
hero_kpi_rationale: The number of Funded Accounts (3.81 million as of December 31, 2025) represents the core of eToro's business model. These active, funded accounts are the direct source of Net Contribution and reflect the company's ability to acquire, convert, and retain retail users across its key markets in Europe, Asia-Pacific, and the Americas.

kpis.name: Active funded accounts
kpis.explanation: Users who have completed KYC/AML, activated their account, deposited funds, executed at least one transaction, and maintain a positive balance.
kpis.description: As of December 31, 2025, eToro had 3.81 million Funded Accounts, up from 3.48 million as of December 31, 2024. This metric represents the most engaged users who generate Net Contribution.
kpis.signal: Steady growth in monetizable user base since Q1 2023

kpis.name: Net Contribution
kpis.explanation: Total revenue and income less cost of revenue from cryptoassets and margin interest expense. Key metric to evaluate net contribution before overhead costs.
kpis.description: For the quarter ended December 31, 2025, Net Contribution was $227 million, down compared to $252 million in Q4 2024, but up 4.6% on a year-over-year average (227M vs 217M in Q1 2025).
kpis.signal: Quarterly volatility linked to market conditions and retail investor sentiment

kpis.name: Total annual trades
kpis.explanation: Total number of orders executed by users covering traditional assets and cryptoassets.
kpis.description: In 2025, users executed 594 million trades, up from 571 million in 2024 and 446 million in 2023. Equity, commodity, and currency trades accounted for 537 million, while cryptoassets accounted for 57 million.
kpis.signal: Sustained retail investor enthusiasm for global markets and cryptoassets

risks.title: Dependence on market volatility and unpredictable fluctuations
risks.summary: eToro's business activity is highly dependent on market conditions (equities, cryptoassets, currencies, commodities). Unpredictable market fluctuations directly impact active user counts, trading volumes, and revenues. For example, recent trade tariffs and geopolitical tensions have created heightened volatility, while prolonged periods of macroeconomic uncertainty reduce user engagement.
risks.score_rationale: Major risk ranked first in Item 1A, highly intense language ("significantly fluctuate", "unpredictable"), stable but structural trend. High category weight: direct impact on trading volumes, funded account count, and revenues.

risks.title: Risk of losses from extreme market movements and risk management
risks.summary: eToro may not always be able to execute or adjust its risk management practices in a timely manner during extreme market movements. Stress tests and VaR analyses cannot fully anticipate extreme conditions. Trading outside regular hours (24/7) increases risks of reduced liquidity, heightened volatility, and wider spreads, potentially leading to significant losses.
risks.score_rationale: Second major detailed risk, highly intense language ("abrupt and erratic", "unable to execute"), stable trend. Critical impact: eToro operates primarily as a principal and holds positions exposed to price fluctuations, counterparty defaults, and liquidity risks.

risks.title: Intense competition from traditional players and fintech across all segments
risks.summary: eToro faces growing competition from large traditional financial institutions (retail banks, neobanks, wealth management), fast-growing fintechs, and international tech-led brokers. Competitors offer wealth management, retirement planning, and advisory services that eToro does not yet provide. Centralized and decentralized exchanges also represent direct competitors in cryptoassets.
risks.score_rationale: Major risk detailed at end of section, intense language ("highly competitive", "expect competition to further intensify"), upward trend. High category weight: direct threat to user retention and market share from banks, neobanks, tech brokers, and crypto exchanges.

risks.title: User and counterparty default risk during periods of volatility
risks.summary: During sudden and significant price movements, leveraged participants may fail to meet their obligations to eToro or other brokers. eToro calculates leverage requirements in real time but faces increased risk of user and counterparty defaults during economic turbulence. Provisions limiting exposure to claims may not be enforceable.
risks.score_rationale: Specific detailed risk, moderately intense language ("increased risk of default"), stable trend but exacerbated by economic turbulence. Material impact: leveraged users may fail to meet obligations, creating risk of cascading defaults.

risks.title: User dissatisfaction, disputes, and reputational damage
risks.summary: The social nature of eToro's platform exposes the company to rapid dissemination of negative user experiences. Investment losses, trade execution failures, or security incidents can trigger mass complaints, litigation, and reputational damage. Even unsuccessful claims are costly to defend and divert management attention.
risks.score_rationale: Major detailed risk, intense language ("highly susceptible", "severely negatively impacted"), stable trend. High category weight: social nature of the platform amplifies negative feedback and may cause user attrition and reduced trading volume.

risks.title: Cybersecurity, personal data, and GDPR/CCPA compliance risks
risks.summary: eToro handles sensitive data (KYC, AML) and user assets, exposing it to cybersecurity incidents, employee misconduct, and data breaches. Non-compliance with GDPR/CCPA can result in substantial regulatory fines. Users may lose trust following security or privacy incidents, affecting retention.
risks.score_rationale: Risk mentioned in forward-looking statements and user retention factors, moderate language ("cybersecurity incidents"), stable but increasing trend. Material impact: loss of user assets, data breaches, regulatory fines, and loss of trust.

risks.title: Regulatory risks and changes in multi-jurisdictional legal frameworks
risks.summary: eToro operates across numerous jurisdictions with divergent and rapidly evolving regulatory frameworks (MiCA for cryptoassets, DSA, GDPR, FCA in the UK, CySEC in Cyprus, CFTC in the US). Regulatory changes may restrict market access, require product modifications, or increase compliance costs. Regulatory inquiries are costly and time-consuming.
risks.score_rationale: Major risk mentioned in forward-looking statements and retention factors, intense language ("changes in regulatory and legal framework", "regulatory inquiries"), upward trend. High category weight: eToro operates across multiple jurisdictions with divergent regulations (MiCA, DSA, FCA, CySEC, CFTC).

risks.title: Dependence on user growth and risk of market saturation
risks.summary: eToro's success depends on its ability to retain existing users and attract new ones. More mature and affluent users may migrate to advanced wealth management platforms. Inflationary pressures reduce disposable income available for investing. Absence of attractive new products or regulatory restrictions may hinder growth and engagement.
risks.score_rationale: Major detailed risk, intense language ("failure to retain existing users or add new users"), stable trend. Material impact: user growth is a key revenue driver; saturation or decline directly affects the viability of the business model.

ai_positioning.summary: No mention of artificial intelligence or AI features in the provided documents. eToro does not position AI as a strategic lever in its recent communications. The focus remains on user collaboration, financial education, and simplified multi-asset access.
evidence: No reference to AI, generative models, or AI APIs
No mention of intelligent features or advanced automation
Focus on copy-trading, product diversification, and user engagement, not AI innovation
